message.content: Logistic regression is a statistical method used for binary classification problems. It models the probability that a given input belongs to one of two classes (e.g., “yes” vs. “no”) by applying the logistic (sigmoid) function to a linear combination of the input features. In other words, it estimates the log‑odds of the outcome as a linear function of the predictors, then transforms those log‑odds into probabilities between 0 and 1. The model is trained by maximizing the likelihood of observing the training data, and it can be extended to multi‑class problems using techniques such as multinomial logistic regression or one‑vs‑rest schemes.
